assessment: This work is a valuable description and analysis of a fossil taxon with importance for understanding the complexities of actinopterygian evolution and is relevant to biologists and paleontologists interested in actinopterygians. Although in many ways Brachydegma raises more questions than it answers, the manuscript represents a substantive contribution to the subject – especially as Brachydegma has been thought by some researchers to occupy a quite different phylogenetic position and thus have a different significance to the overall story.
affiliation: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
